text:
maria: Observed a p99 spike on prod after yesterday's kernel swap + microbatch sizing change. p50 and p95 look fine, but p99 jumped ~420ms on long-context requests. Repro steps and perf dump below, any quick mitigations? :thinking:

maria: repro (short): run loadtester with --seq-len=2048, --batch-target=12, model=redwood-large-quant, kernel=opt_v2_swap. Profiling snippet: 
```
[profiling] serving_latency: p50=18ms p95=120ms p99=560ms
[kernel] opt_v2_swap: init_latency=42ms, first-token=120ms, steady-token=8ms
[queue] microbatch_depth: mean=4, max=18, tail_shed=3
[kvcache] miss_rate=0.12, eviction_count=430
```

maria: My immediate thought: we need a guardrail to prevent a few huge contexts from blowing the tail. Options: per-route max_tokens cap, early truncation of input prompts, or a dynamic short-response fallback when queue depth > X. Thoughts?

chad: +1 on dynamic fallback. We had an incident last quarter where a small fraction of long inputs queued and degraded p99 for everyone. Could we implement an in-runtime "response_slice" mode that truncates generation after N tokens when queue_depth_high?

anita: We can also adjust KV cache eviction ordering to prefer evicting large KV entries first (based on seq_len). That should help memory pressure and reduce kernel init stalls for swapped kernels. Currently eviction is LRU by request id.

kyle: Quick data point: from today's heap dump, kernel swap path causes a 30-50ms per-request bump on first few requests if KV miss rate > 0.1. Combined with microbatching, tails amplify. Suggest two-pronged approach: 1) immediate config changes (max_tokens / timeout), 2) short-term runtime patch to abort long generations when latency budget exhausted.

maria: For (1) what values are safe? I'm thinking per-route: "max_tokens": 512 for chat endpoints with long contexts, and a separate server-side `generation_timeout_ms` default 2000ms. That would stop runaway completions. Wouldn't that break some customers?

chad: We should make it opt-out by default for enterprise tiers and opt-in for dev. But we can roll a protective default for public endpoints: if queue_depth > 8 OR kv_miss_rate > 0.2 then apply enforcement. Pseudocode: 
```json
{
  "route_protection": {
    "enabled": true,
    "queue_threshold": 8,
    "kv_miss_threshold": 0.2,
    "max_tokens_override": 512,
    "generation_timeout_ms": 2000,
    "truncate_policy": "prefer_input_truncate"
  }
}
```

anita: Regarding truncate_policy, prefer_input_truncate means we trim the prompt (drop earliest frames) before cutting completion length — that preserves reply content but may lose context. We should allow per-workload choice because retrieval-heavy apps will break if you trim inputs.

maria: Good call. For kernel selection: can we fall back to opt_v1 (no swap) when microbatch_depth exceeds X? That avoids the init penalty but costs more memory. Kernel selection policy example idea: 
```text
if microbatch_depth > 10 and kv_miss_rate > 0.15:
  route.kernel_preference = [opt_v1, opt_v2_swap]
else:
  route.kernel_preference = [opt_v2_swap, opt_v1]
```

kyle: Implementation note: switching kernel preference is cheap in the control plane but we need to ensure in-flight minibatches drain cleanly. Also we should add a soft timeout on kernel init path: kernel_init_timeout_ms=150. If swap takes longer, abort and retry with fallback kernel. That gives a deterministic tail bound.

maria: I like adding kernel_init_timeout + generation_timeout. That aligns with our SLOs. We should document expected side-effects (more memory use, slightly higher steady-state cost).

chad: Small experiment suggestion before rollout: add a canary flag `protect_tail_v2` on a subset of hosts and run 24h with high long-context synthetic traffic. Measure p99 delta and token-cost delta. If p99 drops without >5% cost increase -> ship.

anita: Also adding KV hinting at request time could help: clients that know they require full history can set header `x-full-kv=true` which pins their context and we don't truncate them when protection is on. That maintains semantics for paying customers.

kyle: For observability we'll need new counters and traces: `protection_applied`, `truncated_tokens`, `kernel_fallback_count`, `kernel_init_timeout_count`. Add them to Console UI per-route so product can see impact.

maria: I'll draft a small RFC for these guardrails. Quick checklist for an immediate hotfix: 
- add generation_timeout_ms default 2000 (server-wide)
- per-route max_tokens_override but only applied when queue_depth/kv_miss triggers
- kernel_init_timeout_ms=150 with fallback to non-swap kernel
- add metrics listed by kyle

chad: I'll own the canary run. Can deploy as feature flag `runtime.tail_protections` to 10% hosts.

deploy-bot: deploy start: runtime-tail-protections-v1 -> canary cluster (10%). initiated by chad at 1928374705

maria: Thanks all — I'll add the RFC link here when drafted. For immediate PRs: anita, can you update eviction logic? kyle, add kernel_init_timeout. chad, run canary and share the loadtest config. :rocket:

kyle: ack, will open PR for kernel_init_timeout and metric hooks.

anita: ack, will prototype eviction-by-seq_len and add `x-full-kv` header handling.

chad: starting canary now, loadtest config: `./loadtest --seq-len-dist=heavy-tail --qps=600 --duration=2h --routes=public-chat` will simulate the worst tails. Will post results. :face_with_monocle:
